title: [MIG-006] Integrate BOOT-037 as the installed standalone Vibez workflow driver
objective: Deliver a usable installed CLI for the complete existing workflow without duplicating the driver already assigned to Fantasy Football #78.
inScope: Integrate the verified #78 implementation through MIG-003's provenance/delta process. #78 remains the single feature owner for setup, issue preparation, self-contained packets, inbox import, errors/repair, PR/CI and explicit next-task handoff. Do not create a second driver or silently mark its acceptance complete. If implementation location changes, reconcile that existing issue/branch before coding.

Adapt its imports and composition to the supported public library/configuration. Align its reusable profile and persistent session/request formats with MIG-002/004. Expose the accepted command surface through the packaged CLI.

Exercise a non-canary task using only the installed artifact: guided setup → issue input → valid registered task → manual role packets/inbox → deterministic validation → required reviews/rework → PR/CI/readiness → authorized controlled completion → reconciliation. Include nonempty requirements and contracts.

Bind PR/publication/GitHub config to the selected consumer and preserve exact-head authorization, durable receipt/attempt identity and errors. Reuse #75's application-service seam where available; HTTP is not required.
Keep manual exchange as a supported adapter and report the remaining human copy/paste steps explicitly. Headless agent execution is owned by AUT-002/003.
**Expected surfaces:** Imported driver/CLI/setup/intake/inbox code, application composition, package exports/assets, profile/session schemas, operator docs and integration tests.
outOfScope: No duplicate #78 feature build, automatic agent launching, weakening of merge authority, or claiming the manual driver is fully autonomous.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-01: The current #78 acceptance mapping and source revision are recorded; any remaining gap is visible and blocks complete-driver acceptance.
AC-02: An operator completes setup and the manual-handoff task/repair journey from the installed CLI without custom JavaScript, source edits or hand-authored request JSON.
AC-03: Requests, imports, resume, PR/CI and completion retain their original identities and gate ownership across restart.
AC-04: A contract-bearing UAT path passes the #76 regression through installed assets and project configuration.
AC-05: CLI and library share configuration/behavior and supported service interfaces; #75 need not depend on source layout.
AC-06: All imported source deltas are accounted for; reusable driver ownership ends in Vibez.
validationPlan:
Run inherited #78 CLI/inbox/driver tests against the actual tarball. Cover partial/duplicate/stale inputs, failed validation/review, restart, changed head, missing CI and withheld merge authority. Use fake external boundaries for deterministic failure tests and clearly separate genuine feature-delivery evidence.

Use applicable repository build/test/schema/contract checks. Retain exact commands/results, package/source/config identities and an acceptance-to-evidence map. Existing or fake-provider fixtures are not independent live review or task-completion evidence. This task is normal feature work, not a new canary requirement.
npm run build; npm test; python schemas/validate_fixtures.py; python schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py; npm run test:adversarial:mutations. Add issue-specific checks before admission.
